questions.question: Explain the difference between simple growth and compound growth in your own words, using money in a bank as an example.
questions.expected_answer: Simple growth means the bank only pays interest on the original amount you put in. Compound growth means the bank pays interest on your original amount AND on the interest you've already earned. It's 'growth on top of growth'.

questions.question: When calculating the value of an investment at the end of Year 2 with compound interest, why don't you calculate the percentage on the original starting amount?
questions.expected_answer: Because in compound interest, your total amount changes every year. For Year 2, you must calculate the interest on the new, bigger total from the end of Year 1, not the original starting amount.

questions.question: In the formula A = P(1 + i)^n, explain what each letter represents in the real world.
questions.expected_answer: A is the final Amount you end up with. P is the Principal, which is the money you started with. i is the interest rate written as a decimal (like 0,08). n is the number of years the money is invested.
